correctness.rationale: The two-sided fair-bit coding of the area-preserving baker map and exact bounded endpoint identity reduce a paired-quantile sum to the reversal-odd m-bit de Bruijn observable. For m<=3 each reverse-odd basis function is an edge gradient. For m=4, a displayed 3-bit vertex potential identifies exactly the kernel of L(h)=h(0010)-h(0011)+h(0101)+h(1011); subtracting L(h)e gives a bounded coboundary. Independently reconstructed all 36 Green-Kubo matrix entries over six basis vectors exactly as vv^T/32, checked the lag covariances (1/8,-1/32,-1/64,0) and all 15 fourth-level cuts. Finite dependence gives the CLT and the gradient yields deterministic bounded sums; the independent tent sampler has iid half-cut differences of variance 1/2. The results are for stationary initialization and exclude binary-expansion branch boundaries.
